Update a fitted mvgam model

Source: R/update.mvgam.R
update.mvgam.Rd

Refit a fitted mvgam object with new data, an updated formula, new priors, different sampler settings or any other argument mvgam() accepts. The signature follows brms::update.brmsfit().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
update(object, formula. = NULL, newdata = NULL, recompile = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

formula.

A new observation formula, or an update to the fitted one such as ~ . + new_term. NULL (the default) keeps object$formula. stats::update.formula() applies the update. ~ . + z, ~ . - z, y2 ~ x and . ~ . all work.

newdata

An optional new training data frame. NULL (the default) keeps object$data. A data argument in ... is an error.

recompile

Optional logical. NULL (the default) and TRUE refit through mvgam(). Both backends cache compiled models by their Stan code. A refit with unchanged code skips compilation. FALSE builds the new Stan code first and compares it with object$stancode. A difference is an error. A refit that passes the check compiles nothing.

...

Any other argument mvgam() accepts, or jsdgam() for a jsdgam fit (e.g. trend_formula, family, prior, chains, iter, warmup, cores, threads, algorithm, backend, silent, seed, init, control). Each value overrides the one inherited from object. A prior joins the priors the original fit set, as Details describes.

Value

A refit mvgam object.

Details

Every mvgam() argument comes from object unless ... overrides it. update(fit, iter = 4000) keeps the original formula, data, family, trend, prior and backend. Only the iteration count changes.

Sampler settings follow brms::update.brmsfit(). chains, iter, warmup, thin and control carry over when the refit keeps the original algorithm. control also needs the original backend. A new iter without a warmup takes the default warmup of iter / 2. control merges entry by entry: update(fit, adapt_delta = 0.99) keeps the original max_treedepth.

New training data passed as newdata keeps the fit's held-out data when that lies after the new training times. Held-out data overlapping them is dropped with a message.

A refit reuses the fitted prior table. The adaptive priors of brms, such as the Intercept prior centred on the response, keep the constants of the original fit. Because the constants stay fixed, a refit on a different newdata window has the same Stan code and reuses the compiled model. lfo_cv() and other workflows that refit many times then repeat only the sampling. An inherited row for a parameter the refit lacks, such as the smooth of a dropped term, is left out of the refit. A prior passed to update() joins the priors the user set on the original fit, as in brms::update.brmsfit(). A new row replaces an old one for the same parameter:

new_priors <- c(
  prior(std_normal(), class = "b"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sigma")
)
refit <- update(mod, prior = new_priors)

A prior change that alters the Stan code recompiles the model. With recompile = FALSE it is an error. stancode(refit) shows the model the refit compiled.

Multivariate fits take a complete new formula as formula.. A formula update written with . is refused, as brms refuses it.

A jsdgam() fit refits through jsdgam() with the arguments the original call evaluated, including factor_formula, n_lv, traits, trait_slopes and phylo. ... overrides any of them.

update() refuses multiple-imputation fits from mvgam_multiple(combine = TRUE). Refit each imputation with mvgam() and pool them again.

See also

loo.mvgam() and loo_compare.mvgam() compare a refit with the original. stancode.mvgam() shows the compiled model. The forecast evaluation article compares competing models by their forecasts.

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_formula(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
# A Poisson GAM without a latent trend. PSIS approximates each
# held-out count of such a model well (see Details of ?loo.mvgam)
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = "None")
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), data = simdat$data_train,
             family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 2 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
# Swap the family for a negative binomial. The formula, priors, data
# and sampler settings carry over
upd <- update(mod, family = negbinomial())
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Compare the two fits by approximate leave-one-out cross-validation.
# The better model has elpd_diff = 0. A difference smaller than about
# two of its standard errors favours neither model
loo_compare(mod, upd)
#>  model elpd_diff se_diff p_worse diag_diff diag_elpd
#>    mod       0.0     0.0      NA                    
#>    upd      -0.3     0.8    0.67   N < 100          
#> 
#> Diagnostic flags present.
#> See ?`loo-glossary` (sections `diag_diff` and `diag_elpd`)
#> or https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo-glossary.html.

# A change of sampler settings alone reuses the compiled model
longer <- update(mod, iter = 3000, recompile = FALSE)
#> Warning: 7 of 3000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
